name: The Tulip Tree of Biscainhos

location.address: Jardim do Palacio dos Biscainhos, Rua dos Biscainhos, Braga

access: Free. The Biscainhos museum garden is open Tuesday to Sunday, 10:00-12:30 and 14:00-17:30 (closed Mondays and some holidays); garden entry is free, just ask at reception. The palace's indoor exhibit is a separate paid ticket (EUR 2), not needed to see the tree.
transport: Central Braga, an easy walk from the historic centre / cathedral.
verify_notes: ICNF register (Aviso n.12 de 21/07/2010, processo KNJ1/554): girth 6.5m, height 27.4m, crown 18m, age_register 270 as of the 2010 measurement -> add ~16 years to 2026, giving roughly 285-290 years now. ominho.pt (2026, Tree of the Year Portugal coverage) independently corroborates: planted in the 18th century during the reign of King Joao V (reigned 1706-1750), consistent with the register's implied planting date (~1740). Same article calls it the largest of its kind in Portugal, ~30m tall with a 19m crown -- flag this as a source disagreement against the register's own 27.4m/18m, both plausible, neither picked as the winner. It is a 2026 finalist (top 10) for Portugal's Arvore do Ano (Tree of the Year), voted on into January 2026, winner to represent Portugal in the European competition -- strong lead-with fact. Stands in the baroque garden of the Palacio dos Biscainhos, now a municipal museum; garden described as ~1 hectare, one of Portugal's most expressive baroque gardens, with an orchard and vegetable garden. Flagged only for the height/crown figure disagreement between sources, not for existence or age.

name: The Cork Oak of Santa Tecla

location.address: Largo de Santa Tecla, Calcada de Santa Tecla, Braga

verified_sources: monumentaltrees.com (French-language record, girth and height match the register exactly, used only as corroboration per the site's rules, not as a source)
access: Free. Stands in Largo de Santa Tecla, a public square used as a neighbourhood gathering space, open at all times.
transport: About 1.5km from central Braga; a 20-25 minute walk, or a short bus/taxi ride.
verify_notes: ICNF register (Aviso n.10 de 05/07/2011, processo KNJ1/610): girth 3.5m, height 15m, crown 21m, age_register 150 as of the 2011 measurement -> add ~15 years to 2026, giving roughly 165 years now. Correio do Minho (local newspaper) covered the 2012 classification ceremony: the parish board pursued official protected status for about six years before succeeding, and the classification was marked on 21 March 2012 (World Forest Day) with a ceremony involving fourth-grade pupils from the nearby EB1 de Santa Tecla school, framed as guardians of the tree. Described in that piece as a landmark and reference point in the neighbourhood's collective memory, with a broad, leafy crown. Stands together with the Three Oaks of Santa Tecla (brg_003) about 60m away in the same square, so the two entries make a short combined stop rather than a detour.

name: The Three Oaks of Santa Tecla

location.address: Largo de Santa Tecla, Calcada de Santa Tecla, Braga

access: Free. Same public square as the Cork Oak of Santa Tecla (brg_002), open at all times.
transport: About 1.5km from central Braga; a 20-25 minute walk, or a short bus/taxi ride.
verify_notes: ICNF registers the three oaks as a single conjunto arboreo, processo KNJ3/073 (Aviso n.12 de 05/07/2011): girth 2.7m, height 16.7m, no crown figure given, age_register 85 as of the 2011 measurement -> add ~15 years to 2026, giving roughly 100 years now. Girth and height are presumably per-tree averages or the largest of the three; the register does not break out individual figures, note this for the writer. Correio do Minho's classification-ceremony article treats the sobreiro and the three oaks as one classification event covering both, describing the oaks as enhancing the square and constituting one of its main attractions, valued for shade in summer and as a community leisure space. Same square as brg_002, about 60m away: a visitor sees both from the same spot, this is a single short stop, not two separate detours. Treated as one collectible entry per the register's own grouping (a conjunto arboreo of 3 specimens at one coordinate), not folded further.

name: The Twin Cedars of Tibaes

location.address: Cerca do Mosteiro de Sao Martinho de Tibaes, Mire de Tibaes, Braga

verified_sources: data/registers/portugal-icnf.json (processo KNJ1/556 and the twinned KNJ1/557)
access: Paid. Inside the monastery's walled grounds (the cerca): a grounds-only ticket is EUR 1.50, or EUR 4.00 for the full monastic complex. Open Tuesday to Sunday, 10:00-19:00 (Apr-Sep) or 10:00-18:00 (Oct-Mar), closed Mondays and a handful of public holidays. Free on the first Sunday of the month for some visitor categories.
transport: About 4.5km northwest of central Braga; no direct city bus to the monastery gate, a taxi or car is the practical route (roughly 10-12 minutes' drive).
verify_notes: TWIN VERDICT: folded into one entry. Two separately registered Himalayan cedars, processo KNJ1/556 (girth 3.55m, height 38m, crown 23m) and KNJ1/557 (girth 3.56m, height 38m, crown 21.3m), both age_register 90 as of the 2010 measurement, standing together beside the monastery lake roughly 10m apart. Near-identical girth (1cm apart) and identical height read as a matched, almost certainly deliberately symmetrical planting, the same design pattern documented for the Biscainhos tulip tree at brg_001, which the register/ominho.pt source says was itself planted as one of an original symmetrical PAIR (companion died late 1970s, replaced 1997) -- monastic and palace gardens in this region evidently favoured paired planting, which supports treating these two as one visitor destination rather than two. A visitor standing at the lake sees both trees as one feature. Coordinates given are the midpoint of the two register points; KNJ1/557 recorded as the folded processo (see data/leads/braga.json). Age: 90 as of 2010 measurement -> add ~16 years, giving roughly 105-106 years by 2026; I have used a rounder 'around 90 years' as a conservative chip label since two independent write-ups (mosteirodetibaes.gov.pt and ominho.pt) both still quote 90 without updating for elapsed time, so the writer should treat 90-105 as the honest range and say so rather than pick one. Official classification 23 July 2010 (Aviso n.13), alongside the pine (brg_005), for their landscape and cultural value. The Cerca was reported closed for works in an older cached search result; the live mosteirodetibaes.gov.pt ticketing page (fetched today) shows the grounds ticket on sale with no closure notice, so I have gone with the live page, but this is worth a fresh check before the story runs given it is a paid, gated site.

name: The Great Pine of Tibaes

location.address: Cerca do Mosteiro de Sao Martinho de Tibaes, Mire de Tibaes, Braga

verified_sources: https://www.publico.pt/2021/03/19/fugas/noticia/alto-pinheiro-portugal-tibaes-1954599 (headline/snippet only, full article blocked automated fetch)
access: Paid. Same walled grounds as the Twin Cedars (brg_004): EUR 1.50 grounds-only or EUR 4.00 full complex, Tuesday-Sunday, closed Mondays; see brg_004 for full hours.
transport: About 4.5km northwest of central Braga; taxi or car, roughly 10-12 minutes' drive.
verify_notes: ICNF register (Aviso n.13 de 23/07/2010, processo KNJ1/555): girth 4.11m, height 47m, crown 26m, age_register 200 as of the 2010 measurement -> add ~16 years to 2026, giving roughly 215 years now. Publico's 2021 Fugas travel feature is headlined 'O mais alto pinheiro de Portugal esta em Tibaes' (Portugal's tallest pine is at Tibaes) -- full article text is blocked by an automated-fetch 403 (Publico is paywalled/blocks scrapers, noted for the blocklist), but the headline and search snippet independently name this tree as the country's tallest pine, corroborating the register's 47m figure from a source that did not derive it from the register. Stands beside the monastery lake, next to the two cedars (brg_004), classified the same day (23 July 2010) for landscape and cultural value. This is the strongest single fact on the whole Braga page: a 47-metre, 200+ year old pine, tallest of its species in the country, inside a working monastery museum most visitors walk past without knowing what they are looking at.

name: The Trees of the Embrace
species: Pedunculate Oak (Quercus robur) and London Plane (Platanus x acerifolia)

location.address: Estacao do Elevador do Bom Jesus do Monte, Braga

access: Free. Standing at the funicular (Elevador do Bom Jesus) station, a public spot at the base of the Bom Jesus do Monte sanctuary hill, open at all times; the funicular itself is a separate paid ride up the hill and not needed to see the trees.
transport: About 5km east of central Braga; city bus to Bom Jesus do Monte, then a short walk to the funicular station.
verify_notes: ABRACO VERDICT: both register entries share the literal name 'arvore do Abraco' (tree of the embrace) in their own official designation text -- KNJ1/558 (plane, girth 2.55m, height 26m, crown 13.2m) is registered as 'platano (arvore do Abraco)' and KNJ1/559 (oak, girth 3.7m, height 25.5m, crown 24.56m) as 'carvalho-roble ... (arvore do Abraco)', both classified together under the same Aviso n.14 de 21/07/2010, both age_register 100 as of that measurement -> add ~16 years, giving roughly 115-116 years now (used 'around a century' as the honest rounder). This is the register's OWN name for the pair, not a coincidence of naming or a guess by us: two different species standing about 20m apart at the funicular station, evidently registered together deliberately as a named twinned feature. ominho.pt's roundup independently confirms both ages (100 each) without adding the name story. I could not find a separate source explaining WHY they are called the embrace (a folk story, intertwined branches, a couple's legend) in the time available -- worth a targeted follow-up search, and the writer should say plainly on the page that the origin of the name is not established rather than invent one. Folded into one entry since they share one register name and one obvious place to stand (the funicular station), coordinates given as the midpoint of the two register points (558 at -8.380999988, 559 at -8.380799988, both 41.55429999).
